title: Internal dual evaluation over a finite-free open
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], M a sheaf of modules, U an open, and I a finite set. Suppose the restriction of M to U is isomorphic to the free sheaf on I [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let V be an open contained in U and put R=O_X(V). Then evaluation at the identity open is an R-linear equivalence from the sections M^\vee(V) of the internal dual [def-pur-sheaf-hom] to Hom_R(M(V),R). Explicitly, there exists c: M^\vee(V) \simeq_R Hom_R(M(V),R) with c(psi)(x)=psi_V(x) for all psi and x. No nonzero-ring, nonempty-open, or positive-rank hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0BRT (lemma-smooth-proper), determinant inversion, expanded by the coordinate arguments in lem-sc-exterior-dual-local-frames proof steps 1-3. The tag was read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BRT; it uses determinant inversion but does not state this coordinate lemma.

proof.text: The finite-free isomorphism gives inclusions S_i and coordinate projections C_i on the localized site over U. Their finite sum of composites C_i followed by S_i is the identity. Restrict these morphisms to the localized site over V. On every W contained in V, naturality of S_i identifies S_i(r) with r times the restriction of m_i=S_i(1) on V. Hence any section x on W is the sum of C_i(x) times the restriction of m_i.

Evaluation of the internal dual at V is linear. If its value on V vanishes, naturality makes its value vanish on every restricted m_i, and the finite expansion above makes the entire localized morphism zero. For a functional l on M(V), the localized morphism sum_i l(m_i) C_i is a preimage under evaluation: its scalar multiplication restricts l(m_i) to W, and at V the expansion of x gives sum_i l(m_i) C_i(x)=l(x), using commutativity of R. This proves bijectivity, so the linear map yields a linear equivalence.

lean.statement:
theorem dual_local_evaluation_equiv (X : Scheme.{u}) (M : X.Modules)
    (U : X.Opens) (I : Type u) [Finite I]
    (e : M.over U ≅ SheafOfModules.free I) (V : X.Opens) (g : V ⟶ U) :
    ∃ c : (dual M).val.obj (op V) ≃ₗ[X.presheaf.obj (op V)]
        Module.Dual (X.presheaf.obj (op V)) (M.val.obj (op V)),
      ∀ (ψ : (dual M).val.obj (op V)) (x : M.val.obj (op V)),
        c ψ x = ψ.app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 V))) x
